model_claims.text: Unary minus tokenization remains unchanged when the minus follows an operator, punctuation, or whitespace.
model_claims.source_quote: Unary minus is lexed exactly as before wherever it follows an operator, punctuation or whitespace: `x = -1`, `values(-1)`, `in (1,-2)`, `a*-1`, `select -1`, and the ambiguous `a -1` all still give an `Integer '-1'`.

model_claims.text: Exponent sign handling is unchanged by the fix.
With the fix, format(..., reindent=True) correctly aligns columns after 'a-1', whereas before it indented the following column too far.
model_claims.source_quote: With `-` now a separate token, `format(..., reindent=True)` aligns the next column after `a-1` correctly. `select a-1, b from t` used to indent `b` one column too far.

model_claims.text: After the fix, a keyword directly followed by a minus without space (e.g., 'select-1') is tokenized as keyword, Operator '-', Integer '1' instead of keyword, Integer '-1'.
model_claims.source_quote: One behavior change to be aware of: a keyword directly followed by a minus with no space (`select-1`, `then-1`) now lexes as keyword, `-`, `1` instead of keyword, `-1`, since a lookbehind can't tell keywords from names.

model_rejected_claims.text: In the original lexer, tokenizing '1-1' produces two integer tokens: '1' and '-1'.
model_rejected_claims.rejected: source_quote not found in the PR text

model_rejected_claims.text: After the fix, tokenizing 'a-1' yields a Name token 'a', an Operator token '-', and an Integer token '1'.
